title: 1. Getting Started
desc: Foodways is a live culinary-heritage intelligence platform combining a browser interface, Supabase database, GIS mapping, AI-assisted discovery, and historical research layers. Start as a Guest to explore, or use Admin Access when you need to curate or edit records.
tips: Guest mode is intended for exploration and reading.
The current production dataset is live in Supabase rather than hard-coded in the page.
Admin tools appear only after successful authentication and authorization.

title: 2. Navigating Foodways
desc: The desktop navigation is organized into Dashboard, Global Map Curate, Global Map AI, and Timeline & Trade Routes. Mobile intentionally simplifies this into Home, Map, AI, and Profile.
tips: Use Dashboard for the overall data picture.
Use Global Map Curate for the published Foodways inventory.
Use Global Map AI for discovery and review of AI-derived culinary signals.
Use Timeline & Trade Routes for historical evidence and route hypotheses.

title: 3. Reading the Intelligence Dashboard
desc: The dashboard is the command-centre view of the live Foodways dataset. It summarizes record volume, geographic coverage, origin links, evidence readiness, media coverage, country footprint, and connection pathways.
tips: KPI values are calculated from the live Supabase inventory.
Use country distribution to spot geographic concentration or gaps.
Use the connection profile to understand how records are currently classified as Trade, Migration, or Colonialism.
Treat dashboard metrics as indicators of the current dataset, not as historical conclusions.

title: 4. Understanding Foodway Connection Pathways
desc: Foodways uses Trade, Migration, and Colonialism to describe selected relationship pathways between culinary traditions. These labels are analytical classifications attached to records and should be supported by evidence.
tips: Trade describes movement connected with exchange, commerce, markets, or trade networks.
Migration describes foodways carried, transformed, or transmitted through population movement.
Colonialism describes foodway relationships shaped by colonial encounters or systems.
A blank connection type is preferable to an unsupported historical claim.

title: 5. Global Map Curate
desc: Global Map Curate is the geographic view of the curated Foodways inventory. Red/local markers represent food records, while gold/origin information can be used to visualize documented or curated lineage relationships.
tips: Open a marker to inspect the corresponding record.
Use the map search field to narrow the visible inventory.
Zoom out for regional patterns and zoom in for local context.
Do not interpret a visual connection as proof unless the record contains supporting evidence.

title: 6. Search & Filtering
desc: Search is designed for moving quickly from a large inventory to a focused research set. Queries can be used with the visible feed and map so textual discovery and spatial exploration work together.
tips: Start with food name, country, or a distinctive keyword.
Search can also help locate records by origin or connection type.
After filtering, inspect the remaining markers to understand the geographic pattern.
Clear the search before making dataset-wide observations.

title: 7. Understanding a Foodways Record
desc: A Foodways record combines identity, geography, lineage, relationship, media, heritage status, narrative description, and research provenance. The live Supabase table is named Heritage Foodways.
tips: Core fields include id, food_name, country, lat, and lng.
Lineage fields include origin_food_name, origin_country, origin_lat, and origin_lng.
Relationship metadata uses connection_type.
Research fields include description, unesco_status, research_links, image_url, youtube_url, and geometry_json.

title: 8. Quality Over Quantity
desc: Foodways prioritizes evidence quality over simply increasing record counts. A smaller set of well-described, traceable records is more useful for heritage research than a large collection of weakly supported claims.
tips: Prefer source-backed records with clear provenance.
Do not invent origins merely to complete a lineage graph.
Leave uncertain fields empty when the evidence is insufficient.
Use human review before promoting an AI-discovered signal into the curated inventory.

title: 9. Provenance & Source Links
desc: Research links are the provenance layer connecting a Foodways record to external evidence. For heritage work, provenance should be preserved even when the narrative is later edited or shortened.
tips: Prefer primary sources, official heritage registers, institutional research, and reputable scholarship.
Keep multiple useful sources when they support different aspects of the record.
Check that URLs still resolve and actually support the statement being made.
Do not treat a source URL alone as proof of every claim inside a record.

title: 10. UNESCO Heritage Records
desc: Foodways can document culinary and food-related Intangible Cultural Heritage elements with explicit UNESCO status. UNESCO status is metadata about heritage recognition, not a blanket verification of every historical statement in the record.
tips: Record the specific UNESCO status or list where appropriate.
Keep the official UNESCO source URL in Research Links.
Do not imply that a food itself is 'UNESCO certified' when UNESCO actually recognizes a practice, tradition, knowledge system, or cultural element.
Distinguish Representative List entries from Urgent Safeguarding List entries.

title: 11. Foodway Lineage & Origins
desc: Origin fields are intended to represent a proposed or documented predecessor, source tradition, or related foodway. They should be used carefully because culinary history is often multi-directional rather than a simple parent-child chain.
tips: Use origin_food_name only when there is a defensible relationship.
Record origin_country and coordinates when the source is geographically meaningful.
Use connection_type to describe the mechanism of connection when supported.
A blank origin is better than a speculative origin.

title: 12. Historical Connection Evidence
desc: Trade, migration, and colonial connections require more than geographic proximity. The strongest records connect a relationship claim to dates, documented movement, archival evidence, scholarship, or other credible sources.
tips: Look for explicit historical documentation before assigning a pathway.
Separate direct evidence from plausible interpretation.
Use confidence language internally when the evidence is incomplete.
Avoid turning a route drawn on a map into a statement of historical fact.

title: 13. Global Map AI
desc: Global Map AI is an exploratory layer built from the culinary signal dataset synchronized from the broader ICH-Radar workflow. It is designed to help researchers discover promising signals, not to automatically publish them.
tips: Browse the AI signals geographically to identify clusters and gaps.
Use the search box to narrow the signal inventory.
Open a signal to inspect its description, cultural significance, related elements, and source URLs.
AI discovery should be treated as candidate generation until a human curator reviews it.

title: 14. Reading an AI Culinary Signal
desc: An AI culinary signal contains discovery metadata that may include a source identifier, element name, country, category, location, description, tags, shared-heritage analysis, completion status, and source URLs.
tips: Completion status describes the state of the AI enrichment pipeline, not historical certainty.
Shared Heritage indicates a detected relationship that still needs human assessment.
Source URLs are the starting point for verification.
Use the signal as a research lead rather than a finished Foodways record.

title: 15. AI Discovery → Human Curation
desc: The core Foodways AI workflow is deliberately human-in-the-loop: AI surfaces possibilities, a human reviews the evidence, and only then can a record be saved to the live Foodways database.
tips: Open a signal and inspect its evidence before selecting Review & Save to Foodways.
Correct the food name, country, coordinates, description, relationship fields, and sources before saving.
Do not copy speculative AI relationships into the final record without checking them.
The curated record becomes part of the live Supabase inventory after successful save.

title: 16. Curation Checklist
desc: Before saving a new record, run a short quality check. The goal is to ensure that the record is geographically sensible, readable, traceable, and appropriately cautious.
tips: Confirm the food/heritage element name is accurate.
Check latitude and longitude against a reliable place reference.
Confirm that the description does not overstate the evidence.
Preserve useful source URLs.
Only assign origin and connection metadata when supported.

title: 17. Admin Login & Authorization
desc: Foodways uses Supabase Auth for browser authentication and Google OAuth for sign-in. A valid session is separate from Foodways Admin permission: the application checks is_foodways_admin before enabling privileged operations.
tips: Signing in proves identity; it does not automatically grant Admin rights.
Admin access is determined by the Foodways authorization data in Supabase.
The application performs a server-backed Admin check before important curation operations.
Never put a Supabase service-role key in frontend code.

title: 18. Creating, Editing & Deleting Records
desc: Authorized Admin users can create, edit, and delete records in the live Heritage Foodways table. CRUD changes are reflected back into the map and dashboard after successful operations.
tips: Review the full record before editing a historical statement.
Use Delete only when you are sure the record should be removed from the live inventory.
After saving, confirm that the record appears in search, feed, and map views.
The current interface generates Foodways-style IDs such as FH001, FH002, and so on.

title: 19. Geographic & Polygon Editing
desc: Foodways supports point-based coordinates and optional geometry data for more detailed geographic representation. The Geo Editor is useful when a heritage practice is associated with a region rather than a single point.
tips: Use a representative point when no defensible precise location exists.
Use geometry_json for richer spatial areas when the source supports them.
Check latitude/longitude order carefully: latitude first, longitude second.
Do not draw a polygon that implies a historical distribution without evidence.

title: 20. Saving to Supabase
desc: Saving is a live database operation. Foodways verifies the authenticated session and Admin status, builds a record matching the Supabase schema, generates the next Foodways identifier, and inserts the record into Heritage Foodways.
tips: If Save fails, read the Supabase error message rather than assuming the data structure is wrong.
Coordinate fields accept decimal values and the editor is designed to tolerate comma or dot decimal notation.
A successful save updates the local map/dashboard state as well as the cloud database.
Refresh the application if another user has changed the dataset concurrently.

title: 21. Supabase as the Live Source
desc: The production Foodways client reads the published inventory from Supabase rather than treating a repository JSON file as the authoritative record store. Repository JSON files are used for research/discovery layers and application guidance.
tips: Live curated records: Supabase Heritage Foodways.
AI discovery layer: ai_culinary.json.
Historical research layer: foodways_timeline_research.json.
Guide/manual content: guides.json.

title: 22. Timeline & Trade Routes
desc: Timeline & Trade Routes is an AI-assisted historical exploration workspace. It presents the earliest supported references available in the research payload, confidence indicators, evidence records, and conceptual route families.
tips: The timeline is cumulative: later years can continue to show earlier evidence.
Use Show undated when you want to keep records without a supported year visible.
Inspect the individual evidence cards instead of reading the route map alone.
Use Refresh Research when a newer research payload has been produced.

title: 23. Confidence & Research Errors
desc: Timeline research separates research strength from historical truth. Confidence can be influenced by the evidence available for date, origin, route, and the overall research result, while errors indicate records that need another research pass.
tips: High confidence is not the same as certainty.
A low-confidence record can still be historically important.
An error means the research pipeline could not produce a satisfactory result, not that the tradition is false.
Human review should focus first on important or high-impact claims.

title: 24. Reading Route Visualizations
desc: The route map uses visual corridors to communicate research hypotheses and contextual relationships. A darker route can represent a currently matched research hypothesis, while a faint dashed corridor can represent contextual heuristics.
tips: Route lines are explanatory research devices, not reconstructed historical tracks.
Click route lines and inspect the associated hypothesis where available.
Do not infer exact travel paths, dates, or distances from a conceptual corridor.
Always cross-check route claims against evidence.

title: 25. Research Notice & Experimental Layer
desc: Foodways labels the timeline and AI-assisted layers as experimental research tools. Their purpose is to accelerate discovery, synthesis, and question formation while preserving a clear boundary between machine inference and verified heritage knowledge.
tips: AI can surface signals, relationships, anomalies, and possible origins.
Humans remain responsible for interpretation and validation.
Evidence is not automatically origin proof.
Earliest supported reference is not automatically the first appearance of a tradition.

title: 26. Exporting Foodways Data
desc: Foodways provides browser-side export tools for different research and interoperability needs. Desktop currently exposes CSV, DCMI-style metadata, GeoJSON, and PDF profile/report outputs.
tips: CSV is useful for spreadsheet analysis and snapshots.
DCMI export is intended for digital-library metadata workflows.
GeoJSON can be opened in GIS software such as ArcGIS or QGIS.
PDF exports are useful for human-readable record profiles and reports.

title: 27. Mobile Experience
desc: Foodways has a dedicated mobile interface designed around touch interaction and simpler navigation. Mobile uses Home, Map, AI, and Profile views and is intentionally less information-dense than desktop.
tips: Home is the compact dashboard/feed experience.
Map starts with a global view so users are not dropped into an overly zoomed region.
AI opens the culinary discovery layer separately from the curated map.
Profile contains authentication, analytics, and export access.

title: 28. Mobile Authentication
desc: Mobile authentication uses the same Supabase account system as desktop. The browser OAuth callback is routed through the Foodways site so authentication parameters are preserved before the mobile interface loads.
tips: Use Admin Access from the mobile landing screen when you need privileged tools.
A signed-in user can still remain a non-Admin viewer.
If OAuth appears stuck, complete the browser redirect before closing the tab.
Admin curation remains subject to the same server-side authorization check.

title: 29. Mobile Profile Analytics
desc: The mobile Profile view includes a compact analytics layer, including the Foodway Connection Pathways profile. Trade, Migration, and Colonialism are calculated from the current live dataset.
tips: The chart is dynamic and updates when the live dataset changes.
Use the pathway split as a descriptive view of current classifications.
A classification chart does not establish historical causality by itself.

title: 30. Foodways Architecture at a Glance
desc: Foodways is intentionally lightweight: a static browser client connects to Supabase for live data and authentication, while research and discovery outputs remain versioned JSON layers in the repository. This creates a practical separation between discovery, research, curation, and published inventory.
tips: Explore: GIS and AI surfaces signals and patterns.
Connect: Supabase provides the live database, authentication, and authorization layer.
Understand: dashboard and analytics turn the inventory into interpretable signals.
Validate: human review controls what becomes part of the curated dataset.

title: 31. Technology Stack
desc: Foodways is built with browser-native technologies including HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, Chart.js, PapaParse, Font Awesome, html2pdf/html2canvas, and the Supabase JavaScript client.
tips: Leaflet powers interactive maps.
Chart.js powers dashboard analytics.
PapaParse supports CSV workflows.
Supabase JS handles authentication and database access.
The static architecture keeps deployment and source inspection simple.

title: 32. Security & Access Model
desc: The application separates frontend visibility from privileged database permissions. Authentication identifies the user, while Supabase authorization and Row Level Security should determine what authenticated users are actually allowed to change.
tips: Publishable browser keys are not equivalent to service-role credentials.
Never embed privileged server credentials in HTML or JavaScript.
Review RLS policies before deploying a new Supabase environment.
Admin UI visibility should never be treated as the only security boundary.

title: 33. Responsible Heritage Use
desc: Foodways is designed as a research accelerator, not an automated historical authority. Digital maps, AI hypotheses, and database classifications should support scholarship rather than replace source criticism, specialist knowledge, or community perspectives.
tips: Distinguish evidence, interpretation, hypothesis, and uncertainty.
Respect community knowledge and cultural sensitivity.
Avoid turning a machine-generated relationship into a definitive historical statement.
Preserve provenance whenever data is reused outside Foodways.

title: 34. Troubleshooting & Diagnostics
desc: Most Foodways issues fall into four areas: browser/session problems, Supabase connectivity or authorization, missing research JSON, or map/rendering state. Use the symptom to identify the layer before changing the code.
tips: No live records usually points to Supabase connection, permissions, or network state.
Blank AI Map usually points to AI JSON loading, coordinate parsing, or map initialization.
Missing Admin tools usually points to authentication or Foodways Admin authorization.
A broken research view can come from an unavailable or malformed research JSON payload.

title: 35. Recommended Research Workflow
desc: For serious use, work from discovery to evidence rather than directly from a map to a conclusion. Foodways works best when each research step leaves a trace that can be reviewed by another person.
tips: 1) Discover a signal or record.
2) Inspect primary and secondary sources.
3) Compare geography, dates, and terminology.
4) Record only defensible relationships.
5) Preserve source links.
6) Mark uncertainty rather than hiding it.
7) Publish or export only after human review.
